channel.title: MIA — Management Intelligence Alert
channel.description: daily selected and enriched macroeconomic and political news

item.title: The EU has told UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham that the UK must raise tariffs on Chinese cars and align more closely with EU trade policy if it wants to avoid "Made in Europe" barriers on key exports, the Financial Times reports.
item.description:
The EU imposes duties of up to 45% on Chinese electric vehicles and is concerned that lower UK tariffs could make Britain a back door into the single market. EU officials said the best solution would be for the UK to join the EU customs union, according to two people familiar with the matter cited by the FT. Burnham has said he would make the case for the UK to be treated as a "trusted partner" under the proposed rules, warning that exclusion could damage the UK car industry. UK Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds said tariffs on Chinese electric vehicles are being kept under review, as EU capitals consider whether UK car exports should get preferential treatment under the EU's planned rules. A Chinese academic quoted by Global Times says the move could be seen as trade pressure. The reporting does not say what tariff level the EU expects from the UK or when the "Made in Europe" rules are to be decided.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The item links two things: EU preferential treatment for UK-built cars, and the UK's own tariff on Chinese vehicles. If the UK moves towards EU tariff levels, on a general reading, UK car production could qualify for the preference, while Chinese brands would lose a price advantage in the UK market. For adhesive technologies the reach is through the vehicle industry on both sides of the Channel, where material and supplier choices follow where assembly stays. Points that may be worth considering include how UK automotive volume would be treated under the planned "Made in Europe" rules, and whether supplier qualification for UK plants depends on EU preference status.

MarketScreener | The News International | Politico Europe | Global Times

item.title: The US and Chinese governments have released product lists under a planned deal to reduce tariffs on about USD 30 billion of imports from each country, and China's Commerce Ministry has confirmed the trade truce runs to 10 January 2027.
item.description:
According to Business Standard, the list for goods that could enter China has 1,619 items, including medical equipment, timber, coal, grains, dairy products, seafood and meat; the list for goods entering the US has 77 entries, including toys, sporting equipment, household products and fireworks. The White House fact sheet describes consensus in the US–China Board of Trade on recommendations for "more favorable tariff treatment" covering USD 30 billion of non-sensitive goods in each direction, naming agricultural products, seafood, wood products, cosmetics and medical devices on the US side, and small appliances, toys, holiday decorations and children's car seats on the Chinese side. According to the fact sheet, China will also import at least 10 million tonnes of US coal a year in 2027 and 2028. China's Commerce Ministry says the first step under the trade council both sides agreed to form is to discuss the reciprocal cut. The reporting does not give the new tariff rates, the date they take effect, or whether the lists are final.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The lists add detail to the arrangement announced at the Washington summit: product lines are now named, though rates and timing are not. For adhesive technologies the reach is through customers' products on both lists — medical devices and cosmetics exported to China, small appliances and household products shipped to the US — rather than through adhesives themselves, which are not named in the reporting. The deal is described as limited to "non-sensitive" goods, so, on a general reading, it leaves the tariffs on industrial and strategic categories unchanged. Points that may be worth considering include whether customer products on either list gain or lose relative to competing origins once rates are published, and how the 10 January 2027 truce date fits with sourcing decisions for next year.

Business Standard | The Statesman | Axios | MarketScreener | Commercial Times

item.title: The Ifo Institute's employment barometer shows that job cuts in the German economy have not continued, with industry still reducing employment but much less than in the past three years.
item.description:
Klaus Wohlrabe, chief statistician at the Ifo Institute, says the downward trend in the labour market has halted for now, but that the economic upswing must continue in length and breadth before jobs are created. Companies remain cautious in their personnel planning. In industry, employment is still declining, but significantly less than in the past three years. Retailers cut more jobs than they created, while among service providers the balance is positive for the first time in a long time. The barometer was compiled for Handelsblatt. The reporting does not give the index level, its change from the previous month, or figures by sector.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The barometer shows the decline in industrial employment slowing rather than ending. For a supplier to German manufacturing, on a general reading, a smaller rate of job cuts in industry is consistent with stabilising output rather than growth; it does not by itself indicate higher demand. It sits alongside the construction order figures in the same week, which point the other way for building. Points that may be worth considering include whether German industrial customers' order patterns show the same stabilisation, and whether the stabilisation in services reaches industrial employment in the coming months.

Handelsblatt

item.title: India's paints sector faces muted demand and margin pressure, with the top listed players down an average 12% over three months, and higher input costs from the crude oil rally expected to weigh on profitability.
item.description:
According to Equirus Securities, demand in the June quarter was supported by calibrated price increases, some pre-buying and channel stocking ahead of price hikes, premiumisation, distribution expansion and healthy project and institutional business. The brokerage expects volume growth in the September quarter to moderate from the June quarter because of monsoon seasonality and the normalisation of dealer inventories. Business Standard reports that the near-term outlook may not improve if current conditions hold. The reporting does not name the companies, give volume or revenue growth figures, or quantify the input-cost increase. It also does not separate decorative paints from industrial coatings. Part of the June-quarter support came from pre-buying and channel stocking ahead of price hikes, according to the brokerage.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The pattern the brokerage describes is, on a general reading, a familiar one: price increases, a quarter lifted by buying ahead of them, and then a slower quarter as inventories normalise. On a general reading, decorative paint and construction chemicals in India share distribution channels and customers, so dealer destocking in paints may also show up in adjacent products sold through the same channels. The brokerage view is a forecast, not a result; the September-quarter results will show whether volumes moderate as expected. Points that may be worth considering include how much of recent Indian sales growth in construction-related products came from price rather than volume, and whether channel inventories in India are above normal after pre-buying.

Business Standard

item.title: China's exports of primary-form plastics rose 35% and exports of basic organic chemicals 25.1% in the first half of 2026, according to China Economic Net.
item.description:
The same report says the growth rate of demand for synthetic fibres and synthetic resins has gradually fallen, while the share of new chemical materials and high-end fine chemicals in the industry's structure continues to rise. The report gives percentages only: it does not give export volumes or values, the comparison period (the report does not say), the destinations, or prices. It also does not say whether the export growth reflects higher output or weaker domestic demand. Cefic head Marco Mensink, in a separate interview with Challenges, names high energy prices and Chinese competition as the drivers of plant closures and job losses in the European chemical industry, and calls a new wave of consolidation "inevitable".

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

Export growth of this size alongside slowing demand growth for fibres and resins points, on a general reading, to Chinese producers placing more basic chemicals and plastics abroad. For buyers of these materials that would, on a general reading, tend to mean more supply options and price pressure on competing origins; for European producers of the same materials it is the competition Cefic describes. For adhesive technologies, on a general reading, many polymers and solvents fall into these categories, so the effect is on the cost and origin mix of raw materials. Points that may be worth considering include which raw material categories in current purchasing have seen Chinese offers gain share, and whether trade-defence cases on basic chemicals are likely to follow export growth of this size.

China Economic Net | Challenges

item.title: The town of Burghausen plans to file a lawsuit against one or more chemical companies in the coming weeks over long-term PFOA contamination, directed among others against the Dyneon group.
item.description:
The town council decided on a so-called performance action at the Traunstein Regional Court, claiming around EUR 1 million in costs already incurred by the town and its municipal companies, including for construction measures. In addition, the town intends to register claims of around EUR 80 million to EUR 100 million against 3M, Dyneon's parent company. The reporting does not describe the contamination itself, say which other companies may be named, give the basis for the EUR 80–100 million estimate, or say what 3M's position is. It also does not say whether other municipalities in the area are considering similar steps.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

On a general reading, PFOA belongs to the PFAS group of very persistent chemicals. The case brings PFAS contamination in Germany into a civil liability claim by a municipality, with a figure attached. On a general reading, claims of this kind are the European counterpart of the PFAS litigation that has already cost producers large sums in the US, and they add a cost of past emissions to the regulatory restriction proposals that already shape the use of fluorinated chemicals. On a general reading, adhesive technologies are users rather than producers of fluorinated substances, where they use them at all, so the exposure runs mainly through supplier continuity and substitution rather than through liability. Points that may be worth considering include which formulations still rely on fluorinated raw materials sourced from sites facing contamination claims, and how substitution timelines compare with the pace of these claims.

Wallstreet:online

item.title: Airbus said on 25 September it had discovered a quality flaw inside the fuselage of hundreds of its best-selling A321neo jets, and kept its target of around 870 deliveries for 2026.
item.description:
According to industry sources cited by BNN Bloomberg, the problem stems from a coat of primer that was incorrectly applied by an Italian supplier. Airbus reaffirmed its delivery target of around 870 aircraft for 2026, compared with 475 handed over between January and August. The reporting does not name the supplier or the fuselage section, say whether aircraft already delivered are affected, describe the fix or its cost, or say whether any safety authority has been involved. It also does not say whether the flaw affects deliveries in the coming months.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

On a general reading, a primer is the base coat that protects the structure and prepares it for the layers applied on top, so a flaw at this step concerns surface treatment and application quality rather than the design of the aircraft. That would put it close to the processes that adhesive technologies and coatings suppliers qualify for aerospace customers. If the industry sources are right, the case shows how an application error at one supplier can reach hundreds of airframes before it is found, which, on a general reading, tends to lead aircraft makers to tighten process audits across their supply chain rather than only at the supplier concerned. Points that may be worth considering include how application of surface treatments is documented and audited at structure suppliers, and whether customers ask for additional verification of coating steps after this case.

BNN Bloomberg

item.title: President Trump has rejected an Iranian proposal for a seven-day pause in fighting and a reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, and said he does not expect a peace agreement until after the US midterm elections on 3 November.
item.description:
Iran presented the proposal at the UN General Assembly; Trump said Iran had "outsmarted themselves" by closing the waterway. On 25 September, US and Iranian negotiators in New York were reported to be exploring a phased path in which Tehran would reopen the Strait and Washington would lift its economic blockade of Iran. The Globe and Mail describes the war as in a quiet phase and reports indications that Trump is holding open new strikes after the midterms; nearly 20 Republican candidates have called for an end to the conflict because of fuel and fertiliser prices. On 28 September, world oil prices rose more than 1% to USD 105 a barrel in early Asian trading after the rejection, according to Kompas. Separately, Kpler data show Saudi crude exports at 6 million barrels a day in September, up almost 80% from 3.4 million in August, after the US military opened a shipping route off the coast of Oman. The reporting does not say how many tankers now use that route.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The rejection removes the nearest prospect of a negotiated reopening, with Trump himself placing any agreement after 3 November. The supply picture is mixed: Saudi exports have recovered sharply through the new route, while the world oil price reported by Kompas stays at about USD 105. For chemical producers, on a general reading, that means the energy and feedstock cost level of recent weeks may stay the cost level for at least the next five weeks rather than a temporary peak. Points that may be worth considering include which contracts and price formulas are tied to Brent through the fourth quarter, and how a post-midterm escalation or settlement would be reflected in supplier price announcements for early 2027.

Herald Scotland | The Globe and Mail | Kompas | Business Recorder | Cnyes

item.title: Order intake in Germany's main construction industry fell 9.2% in July 2026 from June, adjusted for calendar and seasonal effects, with declines in both building construction and civil engineering.
item.description:
Building construction, which is dominated by housing, fell 8.4% and civil engineering, which includes roads and bridges, fell 10%. In the less volatile May-to-July period, orders were still 2.7% higher than in the three months before. Felix Pakleppa, chief executive of the German Construction Industry Federation (ZDB), says residential construction continues to make no progress and that a setback is looming at the turn of the year: the special funding for EH-55 new buildings expires by the end of 2026 at the latest, budget cuts for new construction are being discussed for 2027, and no one knows what funding will look like from January. A funding gap until summer 2027 cannot be ruled out, he says. Separately, Construction Minister Verena Hubertz says housing construction can be boosted by lowering building costs without compromising quality, citing a Hamburg model project. The reporting does not give order values or a year-on-year comparison.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The monthly fall is large, but the three-month figure shows orders still slightly higher than in the preceding quarter, so the July number reads as a setback rather than a new trend on its own. The forward-looking point is the ZDB's: a possible gap in new-build funding from January could reach residential orders in the first half of 2027. On a general reading, construction orders lead building activity by several months, which is where demand for construction and flooring adhesives and related products follows. Points that may be worth considering include how much of German construction demand depends on subsidised new-build programmes, and whether renovation activity would absorb any slack from a new-build funding gap.

Süddeutsche Zeitung | Handelsblatt | Süddeutsche Zeitung

item.title: Pharmacists at Tan Tock Seng Hospital have redesigned the medication box as a single-material paper box without its plastic window, and every Singapore hospital and polyclinic is progressively adopting the design.
item.description:
The previous box had a small plastic window on the front; the new one is paper only. With adoption across Singapore's hospitals and polyclinics, an estimated 4.36 million boxes a year can go into the blue recycling bins in housing estates and public spaces. The change is expected to cut about 4,600 kg of carbon emissions and about 1,837 kg of plastic a year, and it also trims packaging costs across the healthcare system without compromising patient safety or pharmacy operations, according to the report. Tan Tock Seng is the flagship hospital of NHG Health. The reporting does not say when adoption will be complete, who manufactures the boxes, how labels and patient information are now attached, or whether the design will be required for suppliers' own pharmaceutical packs.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The volume is limited to one health system, but, on a general reading, the design logic is the one recyclability rules push across packaging: removing a second material so the whole pack enters one recycling stream. A windowed carton is, on a general reading, assembled by bonding a film patch to the board, so dropping the window removes a film and the bond that holds it, while a paper carton would typically still need closure and labelling adhesives compatible with paper recycling. The item also suggests a buyer — here a public health system — setting the pack design itself rather than leaving it to suppliers. Points that may be worth considering include where other public healthcare buyers are moving to mono-material packs, and how recycling compatibility of adhesives is documented in pharmaceutical and healthcare packaging specifications.

The Straits Times

item.title: EU energy commissioner Dan Jorgensen says the bloc faces an energy price crisis from the Iran war's effect on oil and gas markets and, in a letter seen by Reuters, urges member states to consider measures to curb energy demand.
item.description:
Jorgensen said the EU is better prepared than in winter 2021, when Russia squeezed Europe's gas supplies by reducing deliveries, but that governments must step up their preparations for this winter. The letter is a request to consider measures, not a measure: it does not, in the reporting available, name which demand-reduction steps are meant, whether they would be voluntary or binding, or which sectors they would cover. Separately, an OECD overview reported by Hürriyet Daily News finds that seven of the ten countries working most actively to contain the economic damage from high fuel prices are EU members, with measures ranging from halved train fares in Lithuania to a delayed demolition of coal-fired power plants in Italy. The EU imports nearly all of its oil and 85% of its natural gas, and imports supply 57% of the bloc's energy needs overall, according to the EU's statistical office. The reporting does not give current gas or power price levels or a date by which member states are to respond.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The new element is that the energy commissioner is asking governments to consider reducing demand ahead of winter. Demand-curbing measures in 2022, on a general reading, took the form of national savings targets and, in some countries, incentives for industrial users to reduce consumption, so the letter points to the kind of decisions that may follow rather than to decisions already taken. On a general reading, for chemical production energy is both a cost and, for gas, a feedstock; for adhesive technologies the exposure runs mainly through the cost of energy-intensive raw materials and site energy, on a general reading. Points that may be worth considering include which member states hosting production have winter demand plans in preparation, and how gas-linked raw material contracts would respond to a coordinated demand-reduction step.

The Hindu BusinessLine | Hürriyet Daily News

item.title: Germany's chemical association VCI welcomes simpler approvals in the German implementation of the EU Industrial Emissions Directive, but warns that a transitional rule could add investment costs.
item.description:
The VCI says the parliamentary procedure achieved important improvements, among them simpler approval procedures and greater use of data and management systems that companies already have. Its criticism is aimed at two points. First, not all the freedoms the directive allows are used in water law; in the Bundesrat procedure, the federal states explicitly demand that the European exceptions also be fully reflected in the Water Resources Act, for example where the location and local environmental conditions justify an exception. Second, a new transitional rule for subsequent orders lets authorities apply new requirements before national implementation is complete. The VCI says this puts legal and planning certainty at risk and can trigger additional investment and adaptation costs. The reporting does not say which water-law exceptions are meant, when the Bundesrat will vote, or which installations or requirements the transitional rule would affect first.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

On a general reading, the Industrial Emissions Directive is the EU law that sets permit conditions for large industrial installations, including chemical plants. The item is about how an EU rule becomes German practice rather than about the rule itself: the VCI's two complaints concern exceptions left unused and requirements that can arrive before the law is final. On a general reading, both reach operators of permitted chemical sites through permit reviews, which is where formulators of adhesive technologies with German production would meet them. The position of the federal states in the Bundesrat, which the VCI cites in support, indicates the water-law point is still open. Points that may be worth considering include which German sites have permit reviews coming up under the new rules, and whether water-related permit conditions at those sites depend on location-based exceptions of the kind the states are asking for.

VCI
